disagreements.topic: Round-4 DCF level, split vs single rate
disagreements.positions: Split-rate DCF/share: agent_1 7.30, agent_2 7.05, agent_3 6.56, agent_4 9.28, agent_5 8.25 (mean 7.69). Single-rate: 6.23, 6.14, 5.33, 7.72, 7.57 (mean 6.60). Uplift from splitting the rate: +1.07, +0.91, +1.23, +1.56, +0.68. Fair values 10.69, 8.5, 7.5, 10.4, 8.26 (mean 9.07).
disagreements.resolution: All five DCFs now value the leases site by site from the inventory figures (BP $296M yr-1, Stingray ~$108M, BL Fluidstack $331M then AI lab $454M, 3% escalators). The contract rates sit in a narrow band (AWS 6.5-6.75%, Fluidstack 7.25-7.75%, AI lab 7.75-8.5%). So the remaining $2.7 spread comes from inputs outside the split: corporate overhead ($110M to $150M, and the rate it is discounted at), the WACC on non-contract flows (8.0% to 9.0%), pipeline value ($0.85B to $1.73B) and net debt ($4.78B to $5.28B at Oct-27). I ran every agent on common financial inputs: 9.0% WACC (3 of 5 agents), $5.0B net debt at 2027-10-01 (the agents' mean, which sits inside the $4.5-5.25B bracket from the 10-Q), 495M shares, and overhead discounted at the contract blend. On that basis the split-rate DCF is $6.32-9.55 (mean $7.42) and the single-rate DCF is $5.09-8.29 (mean $6.21).
disagreements.evidence: Agent discounting/fair_value blocks; 10-Q Q2-26 balance sheet (cash $831.8M, restricted $3,188.5M current / $539.5M noncurrent; debt principal $6,015.5M per Q2-26 deck); supervisor arithmetic below.

disagreements.topic: Corporate overhead level and discount rate
disagreements.positions: agent_1 $150M (cash $113M + $37M normalized SBC) at 6.9% (-$2.82B); agent_3 $130M at 7.0% (-$2.13B); agent_2 $115M at 7.3% (-$1.45B); agent_5 $115M allocated pro rata to each stream; agent_4 $110M perpetual at its 9.0% WACC (-$1.72B) while its contract revenue is at 6.5-8.5%.
disagreements.resolution: The 10-Q settles the cash figure: comp $42.4M + G&A $16.5M - SBC $30.1M = ~$28.7M/qtr, or ~$115M/yr. Q2-26 SBC itself runs at ~$120M/yr, so leaving future SBC out entirely (agents 2, 4, 5) flatters value. Adding a normalized ~$35M/yr would cost those agents ~-$1.1/share. That is judgment, so I report it as a sensitivity and do not apply it. agent_4 discounts the fixed overhead at 9% while discounting the revenue it supports at 6.5-8.5%. That mismatch inflates value. Re-discounted at the contract blend it costs ~-$0.3/share, and I apply that. In agent_4's SOTP the overhead is capitalized at 8x against ~14x on NOI, a further -$1.33/share on that method.
disagreements.evidence: 10-Q Q2-26 income statement (comp $42,359K, G&A $16,479K, SBC $30,119K); agent_4 SOTP inputs.

disagreements.topic: Contract discount rates: anchoring and the 10-yr yield
disagreements.positions: Every agent anchors on the secured notes: Black Pearl 6.125% and Stingray 6.000% (Ba2/BB-, AWS lease guaranteed by Amazon.com AA/A1) and Cipher Compute 7.125% (Ba3/BB-, Fluidstack with ~45% Google backstop). All five quote the 10-yr at 5.24% and put the notes ~+80-90bp (AWS) and ~+190bp (Fluidstack) over it.
disagreements.resolution: The coupons, maturities and ratings check out (Q2-26 deck capital-structure slide). The 10-yr was 5.12% on 2026-10-01 (5.19% on 09-30), not 5.24%, so the stated spreads are ~12bp too narrow. Against maturity-matched Treasuries (5-yr 5.09% on 09-30) the notes sit ~+95-105bp (AWS) and ~+205bp (Fluidstack). The rates the agents use are anchored on the coupons, not on the Treasury figure, so none changes. 6.5% for AWS term cash flows is UST+~140bp: sound, given a 2031 note maturity against a 2042 lease end, the equity-slice operating risk and an AA guarantor. 7.25-7.75% for the Fluidstack term is sound. agent_1's 7.25% is only +12bp over a 2030 note for a term to 2037, the aggressive end, but it adds an explicit refresh-default term. The AI-lab years are a binding commitment, not a signed lease, with an unrated, unnamed tenant. All agents correctly price them between the Fluidstack rate and WACC, with a 10-12.5% expected loss. Every agent keeps post-contract, renewal, pipeline and terminal flows at WACC.
disagreements.evidence: Q2-26 deck (Cipher Compute $1,733MM 7.125% 11/15/30 Ba3/BB-; Black Pearl $2,000MM 6.125% 02/15/31 Ba2/BB-; Stingray $810MM 6.000% 06/15/31 Ba2/BB-); US Treasury daily par yield curve, 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-01.

disagreements.topic: Pipeline value per IT MW and probabilities
disagreements.positions: NPV per IT MW net of capex at signing/lease start: agent_4 $5.6M; agent_1 $4.0M near-term / $3.0M GW-scale; agent_2 ~$4.2M x 0.85 dilution; agent_3 $2.9-3.1M near-term, $1.65M Batch Zero, $1.3M 2030+; agent_5 $2.63M. Totals $0.85B (agent_3) to $1.73B (agent_4); mean ~$1.2B. Probabilities: Odessa HPC 25-45%, Reveille 40-50%, Ulysses 35-45%, Batch Zero 8-20%, 2030+ 4-12%.
disagreements.resolution: I rebuilt the NPV per IT MW: $1.40M rent, 3% escalators, 15 years, the shared renewal mechanics and $10.5M capex 1 year ahead at 9%. That gives ~$6.3M at lease start, $4.7M with 2 years of build lead and $11M capex, and ~$4.4M on agent_5's inputs. So agent_4's $5.6M follows from its own inputs and is not an arithmetic error. It sits at the high end because it carries no overhead or financing friction beyond 2% and uses capex at Stingray's $10.5M despite the Barber Lake overrun. agent_3's GW-scale $1.3-1.65M is the low end. This is judgment the evidence cannot settle, so I keep each agent's pipeline. No signed lease exists for any pipeline site.
disagreements.evidence: Supervisor scratch pipe.py; agent site_coverage rows.

disagreements.topic: Net debt at the valuation date
disagreements.positions: agent_1 $4.855B (Sep-27, credits +$0.1B interim cash flow, no contingency); agent_2 $4.882B today / $4.78B Oct-27; agent_3 $5.15B today / ~$4.95B Oct-27; agent_4 $5.28B (Oct-27, +$0.2B contingency, no interim credit); agent_5 $5.105B.
disagreements.resolution: Primary build-up: debt principal $6,015.5M less the $172.5M deep-in-the-money 2030 converts (in shares) = $5,843M; less cash $832M, BTC ~$38M and ~$0.4B of the $539.5M noncurrent restricted cash; plus the $359.3M Barber Lake overrun layer = ~$4.93B. Then -$0 to -$0.37B depending on whether the $373M of current restricted cash above commitments plus AP is truly spare, +$0-0.2B contingency, and ~+$0.1B of Oct-26 to Sep-27 free cash after coupons. That gives ~$4.5-5.25B. I use $5.0B (the agents' Oct-27 mean). agent_1 and agent_2 are ~$0.15-0.2B light (no contingency for further overruns). agent_4 is ~$0.28B heavy (contingency with no interim credit).
disagreements.evidence: 10-Q Q2-26 balance sheet; Q2-26 deck debt table; 8-K 2026-09-25 ($359.3M layer).

disagreements.positions: All five now carry one row per inventory site: 14 sites plus the sold WindHQ stakes. agent_4 splits Odessa into a mining row and an HPC-option row, sequential in time.
disagreements.resolution: Checked row by row. Every agent has the right MW (gross / 216, 207, 70 IT), tenant (AWS on Black Pearl and Stingray; Fluidstack then the AI lab on Barber Lake), contract terms and timing (8-K hall dates for Barber Lake), payment direction (tenants and the Google backstop pay Cipher; Cipher pays Luminant and the first $359.3M of overrun), Colchis at 76%, the sold stakes removed with the Canaan shares credited once, and pipeline probability-weighted net of capex. No MW is double counted. Black Pearl mining ended before the HPC retrofit (10-Q: 'was previously used for bitcoin mining'), and Odessa mining and HPC are exclusive branches. Residual slips are small: agent_2 ends Odessa mining at the Jul-2027 PPA date, though the PPA auto-renews annually; agents 2 and 4 show the sold-JV row at $0.04 with probability 0 although the value sits in net debt; agent_3 keeps a stale weight-0 'pipeline option' method that still says 'rest ~0'. None moves value by more than ~$0.05/share. Two inventory conflicts are settled from the 10-Q: Odessa is a finance lease with Luminant affiliates (commenced 2022-11-22), not owned land, and Colchis is 76% (redeemable NCI $25.7M). Canaan closed at $0.34 on 2026-10-01, so the $18M credit is right.
disagreements.evidence: sites.md / sites.json; 10-Q Q2-26 (Combined Luminant Lease 'classified as a finance lease'; Colchis 76%; Canaan 806,439,900 shares carried at $34.5M); Twelve Data CAN quote.

disagreements.topic: Inconsistent rates inside the non-DCF methods
disagreements.positions: agent_1 SOTP: one 6.5% cap on all $718M of 2028 NOI, Barber Lake included, and overhead capitalized at 10x (vs ~15.4x on NOI). agent_4 SOTP: stale deck 2028 NOI of $727M (site-built ~$702-718M) and overhead at 8x (vs ~14x on NOI). agent_3 NAV (6.5% AWS / 7.5% BL, overhead at 7%) and the EV/EBITDA methods of agents 2 and 5 are internally consistent.
disagreements.resolution: These carry the high fair values. agent_1's own split DCF prices Barber Lake 75-150bp above AWS. A 7.5% cap on ~$300M of BL NOI is -$1.24/share, and overhead at the NOI multiple is -$1.63/share, so its SOTP goes 12.81 -> ~9.94. agent_4's SOTP goes 12.2 -> ~10.3 (-$0.57 for NOI, -$1.33 for overhead). Net effect on fair value: agent_1 -1.0, agent_4 -0.76.
disagreements.evidence: Agent fair_value.methods inputs; inventory flag on the stale Q2-26 NOI schedule.

disagreements.positions: All five agree: no Q3 print before Nov 1 (Q3-25 was Nov 3), first Barber Lake rent in Q4-26, Black Pearl DH2 targeted Oct-31, the Oct-28 FOMC and late-October hyperscaler capex prints. The 1-month ladders are nearly identical.

one_month_reasoning: No CIFR earnings before Oct 31 (Q3 most likely the first week of November). Barber Lake first rent (Q4-26), Black Pearl DH2 (Oct-31), the Oct-28 FOMC and hyperscaler capex prints are the window's drivers. Nothing in the site or discount-rate work changes a one-month distribution, so I keep the agents' near-identical mean, centered on spot.
confidence_reason: My checks settled facts and inconsistencies that move fair value (normalized DCF mean $7.42 split / $6.21 single; reconciled fair value $8.6 vs the $9.07 mean) but do not settle what moves the 12-month price: new lease signings, ERCOT Batch Zero and AI-infrastructure beta. The direction (slightly lower) is clear, but how the value maps to price is not, so I keep the mean ladder.
thesis_break_reason: On common inputs, contracted-only split-rate value is ~$4.4-6.0/share (mean ~$5.0). $7 is that plus ~$1B of pipeline, slightly below the agents' ~$1.2B mean. A sustained close below $7 most likely means the market is impairing signed leases (Fluidstack stress beyond the ~$1.73B Google backstop, Barber Lake overruns past the $359.3M layer, a forced parent raise), not only pricing out the pipeline. Agents' mean is 6.95.
key_drivers: Contracted value is now well pinned down: site-level leases with split rates give contracted-only equity of ~$4.4-6.0/share. At $15.46, roughly two-thirds of the price rests on unsigned pipeline and multiple expansion.

Corporate overhead is now the single largest DCF swing: cash ~$115M/yr (10-Q). Whether future SBC (running ~$120M/yr in Q2-26) is charged is worth ~$1.1/share, and discounting it at WACC rather than the contract blend another ~$0.3-0.6.

Pipeline value ($0.85-1.73B, ~$1.7-3.5/share) rests on NPV per IT MW ($1.3-5.6M) and signing odds. Near-term catalysts are an Odessa, Reveille or Ulysses lease and ERCOT Batch Zero results (~Apr-2027).

Contract discount rates are anchored on Cipher's own secured notes (6.0-6.125% AWS, 7.125% Fluidstack). Splitting the rate adds only ~$0.7-1.6/share, because post-expiry, pipeline and overhead dominate the residual.
Rates (10-yr 5.12%, not 5.24%) and AI-infrastructure sector beta dominate the 12-month distribution.

fair_value.reason: Agent mean 9.07. Corrections on common inputs (9.0% WACC for non-contract flows, $5.0B net debt at Oct-27, 495M shares, overhead at the contract blend) plus method consistency: agent_1 10.69 -> ~9.40 (net debt -0.29/share; SOTP Barber Lake cap 6.5% -> 7.5% and overhead capitalized at the NOI multiple, SOTP 12.81 -> 9.94); agent_2 8.5 -> ~7.85 (WACC 8.5% -> 9.0%, net debt +$0.22B); agent_3 7.5 -> ~7.40 (net debt); agent_4 10.4 -> ~10.08 (net debt +0.57/share, overhead at contract blend -0.30, SOTP NOI $727M -> ~$707M and overhead 8x -> ~14x); agent_5 8.26 -> ~8.05 (WACC 8.0% -> 9.0%, net debt). Mean ~$8.56, about 45% below spot. Charging ~$35M/yr of future SBC to agents 2-5 would take ~$0.6 off.

missed: SOTP uses one 6.5% cap on all 2028 NOI, including Barber Lake, which your own DCF discounts at 7.25-8.0%. A 7.5% cap on ~$300M of BL NOI is -$1.24/share. Overhead is capitalized at 10x against a ~15.4x NOI multiple (-$1.63/share).
Net debt of $4.855B carries no contingency for further Barber Lake overruns beyond the $359.3M layer, while it credits +$0.1B of interim cash. Peers bracket $4.95-5.28B.
The 10-yr was 5.12% on 2026-10-01 (Treasury), not 5.24%. Your Fluidstack rate (7.25%) is only +12bp over 2030 notes for a term running to 2037.
feedback_for_agents.revisit: Split the SOTP cap by credit, as in your DCF, and capitalize overhead at the NOI multiple. Add a ~$0.15B overrun contingency. 18x EBITDA is above peers' 14-15x; justify it or trim.

missed: Odessa mining is cut off at the Jul-2027 PPA date, but the Luminant PPA auto-renews annually with 6-month notice (inventory, 10-Q). Small.
Overhead ($115M) charges no future SBC, which runs at ~$120M/yr in Q2-26 (10-Q). About -$1.1/share if ~$35M/yr is normalized.
Your 8.5% WACC is the second lowest. On a 9.0% WACC your split DCF is ~$6.8 before the net-debt normalization.
feedback_for_agents.revisit: Decide explicitly on future SBC. Show the DCF at a 9% WACC. Net debt at Oct-27 ($4.78B) has no contingency.

missed: The 'other' method with weight 0 still carries the stale round-3 pipeline bucket ('rest ~0'), which contradicts your site-by-site $854M. Remove it.

Your Batch Zero and 2030+ NPV per IT MW ($1.3-1.65M) is the lowest of the five. With the shared renewal mechanics, a lease at $1.45M/IT MW against $12M capex nets ~$3-4M at lease start before signing delay.
feedback_for_agents.revisit: Recheck the GW-scale NPV per IT MW (capex timing and equity-raise friction). Otherwise the site coverage and split rates are sound.

missed: Overhead ($110M) is discounted at the 9% WACC while the revenue it supports is at 6.5-8.5%. That inflates the split DCF by ~$0.3/share. Peers discount it at the contract blend or allocate it.
The SOTP uses the stale deck 2028 NOI of $727M (site-built ~$702-718M) and capitalizes overhead at 8x against a ~14x NOI multiple: -$1.9/share on that method.
Net debt adds a $0.2B contingency but credits no interim Oct-26 to Sep-27 cash (~+$0.1B). The pipeline NPV of $5.6M/IT MW is the highest, with no overhead or financing friction beyond 2%.
feedback_for_agents.revisit: Make the overhead treatment consistent between the DCF and SOTP. Use site-built NOI. Reconsider pipeline capex ($10.5M/IT MW looks light after the Barber Lake overrun).

missed: The 8.0% WACC on post-contract, terminal and pipeline flows is the lowest of the five: 10-yr 5.12% + ~290bp for a 112%-vol, levered developer. At 9.0% your split DCF is ~$7.5.
Overhead ($115M) charges no future SBC (Q2-26 SBC ~$120M/yr annualized).
Your AI-lab rate (7.75%) is only 25bp below your WACC. Fine, but the contract rate then does little work.
feedback_for_agents.revisit: Justify the 8% WACC against the 9% used by three peers, or move it. State a policy on future SBC.
